EPCK.title: A pawn gives check, and the only way out is en passant #shorts
EPCK.desc:
Black's pawn jumps from d7 to d5 and checks the white king on e4. The king can't take it, because the pawn is protected, and every square around the king is covered. But the pawn jumped past the white pawn on e5, so White takes it en passant. En passant is a normal capture, so it can get you out of check.

Did you know en passant can get you out of check?

#chess #enpassant #chessrules

EPNW.title: He waited one move to take en passant, and now it is illegal #shorts
EPNW.desc:
Black's pawn jumps two squares and lands right next to White's pawn. Right then, White could take it en passant. But he plays another move first, Black replies, and the chance is gone: en passant is only allowed on the very next move.

Did you know en passant expires?

#chess #enpassant #chessrules
EPNW.tags: chess, chess shorts, en passant, chess rules, illegal move, chess for beginners, chess tips
EPNW.ig:
White waited one move to take en passant, and now it is illegal. Did you know en passant expires?

DSRK.title: This rook wants to be taken, and it saves the game #shorts
DSRK.desc:
Black is a queen up and about to make another one, and White's king can't move. So the rook checks the black king from the 7th row, again and again. If Black takes it, White has no legal move left: stalemate, a draw. If the king runs, the rook follows him along the row. Even the queen taking it is stalemate.

Have you ever been saved by a crazy rook?

#chess #stalemate #chessrules
DSRK.tags: chess, chess shorts, desperado rook, stalemate, chess swindle, chess rules, perpetual check
DSRK.ig:
This rook wants to be taken, and that is how White saves the game. Have you ever been saved by a crazy rook?

#chess #stalemate #chessrules #chesstactics #draw

PNST.title: Black still has a knight, and it is stalemate #shorts
PNST.desc:
White's king steps to f7, and the black king has no square left. The knight looks free to move, but it's pinned to its own king by the bishop on c3: moving it would put the king in check, so it's not a legal move. No legal moves and no check: stalemate, a draw.

Would you have counted the knight?

#chess #stalemate #chessrules
PNST.tags: chess, chess shorts, stalemate, pin, chess rules, chess endgame, chess mistakes
PNST.ig:
Black still has a knight, and it is stalemate. Would you have counted the knight?

#chess #stalemate #chessrules #chessendgame #pin

F50M.title: A whole rook up, and the game ends in a draw #shorts
F50M.desc:
White checks and checks but never finds the mate. Fifty moves go by with no capture and no pawn move, and a draw can be claimed. After seventy-five such moves, the game is a draw even if nobody claims it. So when you're winning, you have fifty moves to finish the job.

Did you know the fifty-move rule?

#chess #chessrules #50moverule

TRBU.title: Whoever has to move here loses the game #shorts
TRBU.desc:
Each king guards its own pawn and attacks the other one, so any king move gives up a pawn. And in chess you can't pass: if it's your turn, you have to move. With White to move, his king steps away, Black takes on e4, and his pawn walks all the way down and becomes a queen. With Black to move, it's the other way round. This position is called the trebuchet.

Did you know this one?

#chess #zugzwang #chessendgame
TRBU.tags: chess, chess shorts, zugzwang, trebuchet, pawn endgame, chess rules, king and pawn
TRBU.ig:
Whoever has to move here loses the game. Did you know this one?

#chess #zugzwang #chessendgame #chessrules #chesstips

Q2QN.title: The queen is still on the board, and he makes a second one #shorts
Q2QN.desc:
Many players think a pawn can only become a piece that was already captured. That's not the rule: a pawn can become any piece except a king, even a second queen. In theory one side could have nine queens at once, and if there's no spare queen in the set, a tournament arbiter will bring you one.

Did you know you can have two queens?

#chess #chessrules #promotion
Q2QN.tags: chess, chess shorts, pawn promotion, two queens, chess rules, chess myths, chess for beginners
Q2QN.ig:
White's queen is still on the board, and he makes a second one. Did you know you can have two queens?

#chess #chessrules #promotion #chessforbeginners #checkmate

UNDN.title: Make a queen and get mated. Make a knight and win #shorts
UNDN.desc:
Black is threatening mate with the queen on d1. If the pawn becomes a queen, Black checks on d1, and it's mate a move later. But a knight on e8 gives check and attacks the black queen too: Black has to move his king, and the knight takes the queen.

Would you have made a knight?

#chess #underpromotion #chesstactics
UNDN.tags: chess, chess shorts, underpromotion, knight fork, chess tactics, pawn promotion, chess puzzle
UNDN.ig:
Make a queen here, and White gets mated. Make a knight, and White wins. Would you have made a knight?

#chess #underpromotion #chesstactics #chesspuzzle #knightfork

CSRB.title: The rook is under attack, and he can still castle #shorts
CSRB.desc:
Many players think an attacked rook can't castle. It can. The castling rules only care about the king: it can't be in check, and it can't cross or land on an attacked square. The rook can be attacked, and on the long side it can even cross an attacked square, like b1.

Did you know this castling rule?

#chess #castling #chessrules
CSRB.tags: chess, chess shorts, castling rules, castling, chess rules, chess myths, chess for beginners
CSRB.ig:
White's rook is under attack, and he can still castle. Did you know this castling rule?

#chess #castling #chessrules #chessforbeginners #chesstips

TCHO.title: He touched the knight, so he had to take it, and lost #shorts
TCHO.desc:
In a real game, if you touch an opponent's piece on purpose, you have to capture it if you can (touch-move). Here only the rook can take the knight, so the rook leaves the back row, and Black's rook drops to e1: checkmate. Keep your hands off the pieces until you've decided.

Did you know the touch-move rule?

#chess #touchmove #chessrules
